title: implement-lightweight-symbol-relocator-and-compat-sealer-for-hetero-gpu-runtime
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Background: Recent rollouts across mixed GPU fleets exposed long cold-start latencies and intermittent symbol-resolution failures when different nodes run heterogeneous combinations of CUDA, Triton and CUTLASS. The dynamic loader spends significant time inspecting large shared-object graphs (~MBs of exported symbols) and occasionally binds to incompatible symbol versions which triggers subtle runtime behavior changes or fallback to slower kernels.

Goal: Implement a small-footprint 'symbol relocator' + 'compat sealer' that precomputes and packages only the symbols a runtime instance actually needs at startup for a given model profile. This reduces dynamic loader scanning, isolates variant symbols (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS), and produces a deterministic artifact that CI can validate. Success criteria: 30-50% reduction in median cold-start time for model workers, <0.1% increase in symbol-resolution failures in canary, deterministic CI validation enabling gated rollouts.

Approach:
1) Static analysis pass at build time (link-time collector) that records symbol usage for each compiled kernel/quantization path. Generate a compact symbol manifest.
2) Relocator generator that emits tiny shim libraries containing only needed symbol stubs and a lightweight resolver that maps them to the full shared object when safe; otherwise triggers a safe fallback path.
3) Compat sealer: deterministic symbol table generator that enforces canonical symbol names/versions required by the runtime. Seal manifests are signed and verified at agent startup when compatibility mode is enabled.
4) Runtime probe changes: add a probe cache keyed by (CUDA-major, Triton-major, CUTLASS-hash, driver-version) to short-circuit expensive probing and reuse prebuilt relocator artifacts.
5) CI & validation harness: new deterministic linking tests, symbol-table diff checks, and a small-scale Hetero-Canary pipeline to validate on mixed GPU types.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind env var REDWOOD_SYMBOL_RELOCATOR=on.
- Canary: start with 1% of dedicated-pool nodes (non-customer-critical workloads) for 48h. Monitor metrics.
- Expand to 10% with extended regression tests for 7d.
- Opt-in for private deployments with customer approval; require signed seal verification in enterprise builds.

Telemetry & KPIs:
- cold_start_median_ms (per model, per node type)
- symbol_resolution_failure_rate
- kernel_fallback_rate (to generic kernels)
- relocator_generation_time (build-side)
- probe_cache_hit_rate

Testing plan: unit tests for manifest generator, integration tests that create synthetic symbol collisions, end-to-end canary with 50 models across mixed GPU types, stress tests that simulate high-concurrency startup. Add fuzz test that mutates symbol manifests to exercise fallback paths.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: incorrect manifest generation could strip needed symbols -> Mitigation: default-to-safe behavior where missing symbol triggers verbose failure mode and automatic rollback; require signed manifests in production.
- Risk: adds complexity to build pipeline -> Mitigation: incremental opt-in in CI, reuse existing binary artifact packaging infra.
- Risk: subtle performance regressions when resolver added -> Mitigation: microbenchmarks and A/B against baseline, time-based rollout.

Open questions:
- Should the relocator support on-disk caching shared between tenants? (privacy implications)
- How to version manifests across runtime-1.x branches? Propose semver-like manifest-compat field.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Symbol+Relocator+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2846
- Canary dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cold-starts/cold-starts-hetero

Next steps: finish manifest generator refactor, land unit tests, wire probe cache TTL, and create the canary job config.
comments: 2025-02-03: Initial spike showed ~42% cold-start reduction on small Llama models using prototype stub libs. Prototype stored prelinked mapping in /var/cache/relocator.

2025-02-14: Design review with infra and security — agreed to require signed manifests for any production rollouts. Security requested a short review; added to security_review_required flag = false for now but will revisit before release.

2025-02-20: Marcus Lee: converted prototype to new packaging format; created relocator generator and added basic CI test. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2846. Requesting review from @NinaPatel and @EthanWu.

2025-02-27: Nina Patel (review): requested clearer fallback semantics and a smoke test to detect missing weak symbols early. Also flagged potential issue with on-disk cache permissions for multi-tenant hosts.

2025-03-01: Marcus Lee: addressed Nina's feedback, added smoke test, and introduced a per-tenant cache namespace to avoid cross-tenant leaks. Pushed updated branch and added canary job manifest. PR updated: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2846#pullrequestreview-52.

2025-03-04: Performance team ran 100-run cold-start benchmark across a T4 / A100 mixed fleet — median improvement 31%, p95 improvement 18%. Next: enable canary on 1% of dedicated pool and collect telemetry for 72h.
notes: Keep symbol-relocator off for hosted-tier during initial canary (avoid customer-facing risk).
Follow up: add manifest-to-artifact signing via existing release keyring.
Coordinate with Dedicated infra team to ensure pre-seeded artifacts available in remote caches for low-bandwidth regions.
